newsitem.title: UK: Major's tax plans cost 13 bln stg a year - Labour.
newsitem.headline: Major's tax plans cost 13 bln stg a year - Labour.

text.p: Tax plans expected to be announced by Britain's ruling Conservatives in its manifesto on Wednesday would cost at least 13 billion pounds ($21.38 billion) a year, Labour's economics spokesman Gordon Brown said.

Commenting on press reports that the centrepiece of the manifesto would be a plan for tax relief for married couples, Brown said that if implemented in full such a plan could cost 5.2 billion pounds a year. ($1=.6080 Pound)

Brown said cutting the basic rate of income tax to 20 percent from 23 percent, one of the Conservatives' aims, would cost another 5.4 billion, the abolition of capital gains tax at least three billion and the abolition of inheritance tax 1.5 billion.
"I challenge John Major to confirm that his tax plans alone now cost at least 13 billion in a full year," Brown said.
"The question Mr Major must answer is:'Where is the money for his tax changes coming from? Why is he risking economic recovery and higher interest rates by a reckless and desperate set of promises?'"
